text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The daughter of former interior minister Mehmet Agar, who resigned over a security scandal, dies of brian tumor.
- Public reaction forces Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party to take a step back in its plan to lift restrictions on females wearing the Islamic headscarf.
- Irregularities appeared in parliamentary vote that cleared Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller of corruption charges. One vote against her was not counted and an MP from her party voted, twice.
- Italy gives conditional support to Turkey's membership of European Union during trip to Rome by Ciller.
- Eighty-eight kg of heroin siezed on a truck with an official registration plate in the southeastern province of Hakkari.
- Islamists set up their own private bodyguard groups in step towards forming private militias.
- Two bids received for the sell-off of 30-40 percent stake of Turkey's leading flat steel producer Eregli Demir ve Celik Fabrikalari A.S.
- Cabinet will discuss draft law on the lifting of a ban on female civil servants wearing the Islamist headscarve.
